metadata.description: Brunswick & Western Railroad and its predecessors and successors: Brunswick - Waycross - Albany, Georgia (~169 mi), drawn by era and operator - Brunswick & Florida 1861-63, Brunswick & Albany 1870/71-1882, Brunswick & Western 1882-88, Plant System 1888-1902, Atlantic Coast Line 1902-67 (Albany-Waycross) and 1902-1910 [OPEN] (Waycross-Brunswick), Seaboard Coast Line 1967-71 (Albany-Waycross).
metadata.colour_normalization: Rule 4: the Brunswick and Albany Railroad and the Brunswick and Western Railroad are the same company renamed after its foreclosure reorganization (Dec 1882) - same road, staff and trains - so both company strings carry one colour, #8E3B5F, new to data/. The Brunswick and Florida (1861-63) is treated as a distinct era/company (line lifted 1863, rebuilt from scratch 1869-70) with its own new colour #4E7FA6. Plant System, Atlantic Coast Line and Seaboard Coast Line colours are pulled programmatically from existing features (plant_system_florida.geojson plant-system-waycross-tampa / acl-waycross-tampa; company "Seaboard Coast Line Railroad").
metadata.ownership_splits: Split at 1882 (B&A -> B&W, label change only, same colour), 1888 (SF&W/Plant control: Plant management ran the trains), 1 July 1902 (ACL purchase), 1 July 1967 (SCL merger, Albany-Waycross only). Waycross-Brunswick and Waycross-Albany are separate features where their dates differ (B&A opening 1870 vs 1871; ACL end 1910 [OPEN] vs 1967).
metadata.omitted: Brunswick & Florida Schlatterville - Glenmore (original main line to the A&G, c.1859-71): no confirmed passenger year - omitted. Graded-but-never-railed extension west of Albany toward Cuthbert/Eufaula: never operated. All freight-only years (Waycross-Brunswick after its unknown pre-1949 passenger end; Albany-Waycross after 1 May 1971) are not drawn.
not_yet_sourced: Waycross-Brunswick (acl-waycross-brunswick): passenger end is OPEN - 1910 is the last confirmed year (Brunswick News 30 Apr 1910); service ended somewhere 1911-1948 (1949 ACL employee timetable shows only a local freight; Feb 1952 Official Guide marks it freight only). Leads: Brunswick News after 1922 on Georgia Historic Newspapers; Georgia PSC / ICC discontinuance filings; a 1930s-40s ACL public timetable. If Fowler's w2 = 1927 working timetable is confirmed for Georgia, the confirmed end moves to 1927 [OPEN].
Brunswick and Western east half (Waycross-Brunswick) 1883-1888: no dated passenger item seen; drawn as interior to continuous operation 1882-1897.
Operator 1871-1873: the State put the Atlantic & Gulf's president in charge on 23 Oct 1871 and the A&G ran the Albany trains from Nov 1871; when that ended is unknown, so no A&G feature is drawn.
Brunswick and Albany 1872-1874: no timetable found (receivership, foreclosure); drawn continuous, neither continuity nor suspension documented.
B&A reopening Brunswick-Tebeauville: RailGa "May 1869" vs Wikipedia May 1870 (dated railhead sequence) - drawn from 1870.
Brunswick and Florida before Aug 1861 (Brunswick-Satilla by 1855, Glenmore c.1859): passenger service not established; drawn from 1861.
Amtrak routing in 1971 (Floridian via Thomasville, not Albany) is general knowledge, not a fetched document.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates.
sources: John Fowler, Georgia Railroads SL 234 (branchline.uk georgiarrs.pdf, 11.10.22), line 12 "ALBANY - BRUNSWICK (ACL)"

Official Guide, Feb 1952 (schedules eff. 30 Sept / 13 Dec 1951): Table 23 "Albany, Waycross and Jacksonville"; Table 25 "Waycross and Brunswick" with index dagger = freight only (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt)
Chronicling America (loc.gov): Marietta Journal 24 Nov 1871, 2 Aug 1872, 12 Sept 1873, 5 Nov 1875; New York Herald 17 Oct 1873; Savannah Morning News 2 Sept 1882; Brunswick News 30 Apr 1910

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap (Overpass, mail.ru mirror) end to end with opstrace: 58.2 mi drawn vs 57.7 mi documented (Official Guide 1952 Table 25, Waycross-Brunswick); Fowler mileposts give 57.7. No straight-line leg. About 53.7 mi on ways tagged old_railway_operator=ACL (CSX Brunswick Subdivision), ~4.6 mi on untagged/abandoned track at Brunswick. The last ~3 mi into Brunswick (Dock Junction - Brunswick) are drawn on the Southern Railway (ex-Macon & Brunswick, now NS Brunswick District) alignment and an abandoned grade into downtown, ending at about the SOU station site: Fowler records the B&W/ACL ran this stretch over the Southern, and the Brunswick terminal itself moved (ACL 1st station Mansfield St; later the SOU station) - the terminal point drawn is approximate to within ~0.5 mi. Waycross is drawn through the modern CSX layout (Rice Yard area), not the 1870s Tebeauville junction with the Atlantic & Gulf. LATER ALIGNMENT THAN ITS ERA: drawn on the modern CSX Brunswick Subdivision, but the 1861-63 Brunswick & Florida track was lifted by the Confederacy in 1863 and the line rebuilt from scratch in 1869-70 by the Brunswick & Albany; the 1861 alignment probably ran close to the rebuilt one but has not been checked, and the Brunswick terminal of the 1860s is not located.

segments.note: Brunswick & Florida trains Brunswick - Tebeauville (No. 9 on the Savannah, Albany & Gulf, now Waycross): schedule effective 27 Aug 1861 (Supt. John Brooks) ran tri-weekly, Brunswick Mon/Wed/Fri and back Tue/Thu/Sat, connecting with the SA&G; "daily connections to Brunswick" advertised at Tebeauville from Oct/Nov 1861 and still on 16 Oct 1862 and 21 July 1863 (Atlantic & Gulf) schedules. Steam: 2 locomotives. Late in 1863 the Confederate government took up the rails for the Du Pont - Live Oak connection; the last train is not dated. The road was renamed Brunswick & Albany on paper in Sept/Dec 1861 but advertised as the B&F through 1863. Line dead 1863-1869 - deliberately not bridged to the B&A features. The original B&F main line Schlatterville - Glenmore (A&G junction), c.1859-71, has no confirmed passenger year and is not drawn. Headway: daily (1440) is the 1861-63 advertised frequency after the first tri-weekly months; estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start from the B&F schedule effective 27 Aug 1861 (Savannah Morning News 27 Aug 1861); end from the A&G schedule effective 21 July 1863 (Savannah Republican 19 July 1863) and the 1863 removal of the rails (csa-railroads.com, Wikipedia, RailGa).

segments.note: Line rebuilt from scratch after the 1863 removal: Wikipedia gives railhead at Waynesville 24 Nov 1869, Satilla 25 Jan 1870, Big Creek (MP 47.5) 10 Mar 1870 and the Atlantic & Gulf junction at Tebeauville May 1870; RailGa says "by May of [1869]" - source conflict, recorded; drawn from 1870, the date the detailed sequence supports. Passenger stops in the 1875 Official Guide (Fowler "y": Randolph, Satilla, Waynesville); B&A trains "for Brunswick ... daily except Sunday" from the junction in Sept 1882. The State of Georgia seized the road 23 Oct 1871 and put the Atlantic & Gulf's president in charge; receivership 1872; sold to German bondholders 16 Oct 1873 (name kept). No timetable found for 1872-74 - neither a suspension nor continuity is documented; drawn continuous. Ends 1882 at the reorganization as the Brunswick & Western (a rename, service continues). Headway: one train a day each way is an estimate from the 1882 "daily except Sunday" advertisement.
sources: Segment-level: start from the dated 1869-70 railhead sequence in Wikipedia (RailGa conflicts: May 1869); 1875 Official Guide stops via Fowler line 12 "y"; end/continuity from Savannah Morning News 2 Sept 1882 p3 (Chronicling America) and the Dec 1882 B&W reorganization (RailGa).

segments.note: First train from Brunswick reached Albany 2 Oct 1871 (Wikipedia; RailGa "October of 1871"); from late Nov 1871 thrice-weekly trains to Albany from the junction - run by the Atlantic & Gulf, whose president the State had put in charge on 23 Oct 1871. When the A&G arrangement ended (1872 receivership? Oct 1873 sale?) is unresolved, so no A&G split is drawn. Part-way service west of Waycross before Oct 1871 is possible but unproven, not drawn. Stops in the 1875 Official Guide (Fowler "y": Junction, Willacoochee, Kirkland, Pearson's, Waresboro, Waycross) and 1880 Guide (Alford, Willacoochee); Sept 1882 B&A trains "leave junction, going west ... daily except Sunday". Graded extension west of Albany toward Cuthbert/Eufaula never carried trains - not drawn. Ends 1882 at the B&W reorganization (rename). Headway: daily (1440) estimated from the 1882 advertisement; thrice weekly at the start.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 2 Oct 1871 first train and Nov 1871 regular trains (Wikipedia, RailGa); 1875/1880 Official Guide stops via Fowler line 12; end from Savannah Morning News 2 Sept 1882 p3 (Chronicling America) and the Dec 1882 reorganization.

segments.note: The Brunswick & Albany reorganized as the Brunswick & Western, Dec 1882 - same road, staff and trains (hence the same colour as the B&A). Marketed as the "Ty-Ty Route to Florida". West half: passenger stops in the 1884 Official Guide (Fowler "q": Red Bluff; 1884 note: Millwood) and 1887 Guide (McDonald's Mill). East half (Waycross - Brunswick): no dated passenger item found for 1883-88 (RailGa's 1886 timetable image link is broken) - drawn because it is interior to a continuously operated line between Sept 1882 (B&A trains to Brunswick) and 1897 (Plant System timetable); see not_yet_sourced. Poor's (via RailGa): 19 passenger cars in 1889. Ends 1888 when H. B. Plant's Savannah, Florida & Western bought control and its management took over (trains continue as the Plant System feature). Headway: daily (1440) is an estimate; unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from the Dec 1882 reorganization and end from the 1888 SF&W purchase of control (RailGa brunwest.html); west-half service from the 1884 and 1887 Official Guides via Fowler line 12. East half 1883-88 NOT confirmed by any dated item.

segments.note: H. B. Plant's Savannah, Florida & Western bought control of the Brunswick & Western in 1888; Plant became president and SF&W general manager H. S. Haines the B&W's GM (RailGa) - so the Plant System ran the trains from 1888 (split here per Rule 4). The B&W was merged into the SF&W in 1901 (no colour change). Whole line in the 1897 Plant System public timetable (Fowler "z": Albany ... Waresboro on the west half; Randolph, Hoboken, Nahunta, Lulaton, Atkinson, Waynesville, Jamaica, Brunswick (Mansfield St) on the east half); west half also in a March 1901 public timetable (Bunn's Mill). Ends 1 July 1902 when the Atlantic Coast Line bought the Plant System (trains continue as the ACL features). Headway: two trains a day each way (720) is an estimate; unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: start from the 1888 SF&W purchase of control (RailGa); whole line confirmed by the 1897 Plant System public timetable (Fowler line 12 "z"); end at the ACL purchase effective 1 July 1902 (Wikipedia; research/branches/atlantic_coast_line_railroad.txt).

segments.note: ACL from its purchase of the Plant System, 1 July 1902 (the "P Line" / Albany Subdivision). The Chicago/Midwest - Florida route: Central of Georgia to Albany, ACL Albany - Waycross - Jacksonville - used by the City of Miami, Dixie Flyer, Flamingo, Seminole and South Wind; three passenger trains each way daily in the 1949 ACL Southern Division employee timetable (Wikipedia). Official Guide Dec 1951 Table 23 "Albany, Waycross and Jacksonville" with the City of Miami (trains 14/15, every third day). Ends 1 July 1967 at the Seaboard Coast Line merger (trains continue as the SCL feature). Headway 480 is the 1949 three-a-day figure applied to the whole span - an estimate; earlier and later frequencies unsourced.
sources: Segment-level: start at the ACL purchase effective 1 July 1902; service confirmed 1949 (ACL employee timetable, via Wikipedia) and Dec 1951 (Official Guide Table 23); end at the SCL merger 1 July 1967.

segments.note: Seaboard Coast Line from the ACL-SAL merger, 1 July 1967. Wikipedia (citing SCL Waycross Division timetables 1967 and 1971): "The City of Miami and the Seminole continued to operate on the Albany Subdivision after the merger ... passenger service was discontinued in 1971" - both trains ended at the Amtrak takeover, last runs 30 Apr / 1 May 1971. Amtrak ran nothing over this line (its Floridian went via Montgomery - Dothan - Thomasville - Waycross; general knowledge, not a fetched document). Freight continues (CSX; Sylvester - Albany Georgia & Florida Railway) - not drawn. Headway: about one train a day each way (1440) is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: start at the SCL merger 1 July 1967; end from SCL Waycross Division timetable 1971 via Wikipedia (passenger service discontinued 1971).

segments.note: ACL from its purchase of the Plant System, 1 July 1902 (the "O Line"). Brunswick News 30 Apr 1910 p8: "Atlantic Coast Line - Excellent Passenger Service", two arrivals and two departures daily at Brunswick, with through connection via Waycross to Port Tampa for Key West and Havana; in 1910 this was the ACL's only line into Brunswick. [OPEN] 1910 is the last CONFIRMED year, NOT a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. It ended somewhere between 1910 and 1949: Fowler's undated "w"/"w2" stops (Coon Hollow, Anguilla, Arco) may mean 1916/1927 working timetables if his South Carolina legend applies in Georgia (unconfirmed); the 1949 ACL employee timetable (via Wikipedia) shows only a local freight; the Feb 1952 Official Guide marks Table 25 freight only, with Brunswick served by Service Bus Lines from Nahunta. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 from the 1910 two-a-day figure; estimate for the other years.
